$metadata.description: Kluvs Design System — canonical design tokens. Platform-agnostic source of truth. Compatible with Style Dictionary v4 ($value / $type / $description format). When syncing a client repo, read this file and propagate changed values to the platform-specific token files (Color.kt, Colors.swift, tailwind.config.js, etc.).

primary.$description: Copper — the only chromatic accent. One per view, on the primary CTA and active state only.

primary-hover.$description: Copper darkened for hover/press states on filled buttons.

primary-light.$description: Copper lightened — use sparingly for tinted backgrounds or soft highlights.

tertiary.$description: Blue-teal — admin role color, info accents.

on-primary.$description: Text/icon color on copper surfaces. Contrast vs primary: 3.53:1 — known exception, see accessibility notes.

warm-dark.$description: Warm near-black surface scale — the canonical dark surface stack for the product UI.

card.$description: Card surface — one step above base.

card-2.$description: Elevated card surface and hairline divider color.

accent-fill.$description: Tinted warm fill for the highlighted Next Discussion card.

foreground-warm.$description: Text and icon colors for use on warm dark surfaces.

primary.$description: Cream — label / variant / accent text on dark (wordmark, avatar initials, member role label, input labels, card subtitles), despite the token name. NOT the primary body text — primary body text on dark surfaces is white (color.content-dark.primary). Inverts to color.warm-dark.base (#140F0D, dark chocolate) on light surfaces — same swap as the surface backgrounds. Contrast vs warm-dark base: 16.32:1 (AAA).

tertiary.$description: Meta text and captions on dark. Contrast vs warm-dark base: 4.94:1 (AA).

placeholder.$description: Input placeholder text on dark. Contrast vs warm-dark base: 3.07:1 (AA UI).

disabled.$description: Disabled text on dark. Contrast vs warm-dark base: 1.90:1 — intentionally inaccessible to signal non-interactivity.

light.$description: Web and auth/marketing surfaces. Cream scale — inverse of the warm-dark scale (chocolate bg / cream text becomes cream bg / chocolate text).

page.$description: Cream — page background. Inverse of color.warm-dark.base (#140F0D) / foreground-warm.primary pairing.

bar.$description: Top bar and sub-bar surface. Inverse of color.warm-dark.bar.

card.$description: Mayonnaise — card surface, lighter than the page. Inverse of color.warm-dark.card being lighter than base.

deep.$description: Deepest cream — nav / chrome surface. Inverse of color.warm-dark.nav.

divider.$description: Warm divider and hairline border on light surfaces. Inverse of color.warm-dark.card-2.

accent-fill.$description: Copper tinted fill on light surfaces. Inverse of color.warm-dark.accent-fill.

foreground-light.$description: Text colors for use on light surfaces. Mirrors foreground-warm 1:1.

primary.$description: Primary text on light. Contrast vs white: 17.40:1 (AAA). Inverse of color.content-dark.primary (white).

secondary.$description: Secondary / supporting text on light. Contrast vs white: 5.74:1 (AA). Inverse of color.content-dark.secondary.

label-variant.$description: Dark Chocolate — label / variant / accent text on light (wordmark, avatar initials, member role label, input labels, card subtitles). Inverse of foreground-warm.primary (cream) — same swap as the surface backgrounds. Contrast vs page (#F2EDE5): 16.32:1 (AAA).

tertiary.$description: Meta text and captions on light. Inverse of foreground-warm.tertiary.

placeholder.$description: Input placeholder text on light. Inverse of foreground-warm.placeholder.

disabled.$description: Disabled text on light — intentionally low-contrast to signal non-interactivity. Inverse of foreground-warm.disabled.

owner.$description: Mustard — Owner role badge. ~7:1 on dark, ~3:1 on light — usable as a graphical badge indicator on both surfaces.

admin.$description: Teal — Admin role badge. AA on light (6.45:1). Known exception on dark (2.95:1) — used as graphical indicator only, never body text.

admin-on-dark.$description: Lighter teal — Admin role *label text* on dark surfaces. Use color.role.admin for the badge/dot, this for adjacent text, since color.role.admin fails AA as text on dark.

member-label.$description: Member role label text — cream (foreground-warm.primary) on dark, inverted to color.warm-dark.base (dark chocolate) on light. Same swap as component.avatar.initials. No longer tied to color.brand.secondary / color.status.success.

danger.$description: Error / danger. AA on dark (5.06:1). Known exception on light (3.76:1) — always used alongside 'Error:' text prefix, never as sole state indicator.

primary-subtle.$description: Copper tinted fill — advisory/warning context boxes (e.g. 'This will disconnect Discord').

primary-border-soft.$description: Copper soft border — pairs with primary-subtle for warning box borders.

danger-subtle.$description: Danger tinted fill — destructive consequence boxes (e.g. 'This will permanently delete').

danger-border-soft.$description: Danger soft border — pairs with danger-subtle for consequence box borders.

success-subtle.$description: Success tinted fill — e.g. pressed 'yes' state in a segmented RSVP/attendance control.

dark-web.$description: Neutral dark surface stack (cool, not warm). Used in kluvs-frontend. Distinguish from the warm-dark stack which has brown-tinted near-blacks.

overlay.$description: Backdrop colors for modal dialogs and drawers.

spacing.$description: 4-unit base scale. Page gutters: space-5 (20px). Card padding: space-4 (16px).

modal.$description: Dialog and sheet container corner radius. Same value as radius.lg — semantic alias for platform engineers.

pill.$description: Avatars, bottom-nav pill, fully rounded elements.

default.$description: House identity easing — used for all transitions.

typography.$description: v2 model (superseding the old tier/scale split, see docs/typography.md for full rationale and the frontend-audit evidence behind it). A typography 'family' is a fixed shape (font-family + weight + default style), given 1-3 named rungs (small/medium/large) where real usage justifies more than one size. Families are named generically (Display, Headline, Title, Body, Caption, Eyebrow, Label, Fine print, Mono) — never after the UI component they happen to appear in — so a given family can be mapped onto new components later without renaming it. Two orthogonal modifiers (feature, highlight) apply on top of specific families instead of being their own named tiers — see 'modifier' below. Numeric values here are the single shared scale: every platform (web, Android, iOS) uses the same numbers for a given rung. Platforms differ in which rungs they reach for, not in what a rung is worth — e.g. only wide web layouts use Display; mobile tops out at Headline. See docs/typography.md 'Cross-platform sizing' for the reasoning.

sans.$description: UI chrome, body text, labels, buttons, and all non-literary content. Loaded via Google Fonts CDN (wght 400;500;700).

serif.$description: Wordmark, display text, headlines, titles, and book titles. Italic used for the 'feature' modifier (book titles, the currently-active/featured item, empty-state copy). Loaded via Google Fonts CDN (wght 400;500;700, italic 400;500). This is the literary register — use for content being read or identified, not UI chrome.

mono.$description: Reserved family for numeric/tabular metadata (dates, ISBNs, IDs) — currently system-stack only, no bundled webfont/typeface chosen yet. Confirmed real usage in kluvs-frontend (DiscussionsTimeline date column, BookInfo ISBN row) but not yet formalized into a dedicated typeface decision.

modifier.$description: Two orthogonal, boolean-ish behaviors layered on top of a family+rung rather than being named tiers of their own. Combining both on the same run of text is untested — no observed case needs it yet.

feature.$description: Roman → italic register flip. Signals 'the featured/current thing' — book titles, the active session/discussion, empty-state headlines, italic asides ('3 books in progress'). Does not change size or weight, only font-style. Applies to: headline, title, caption. Does not apply to: display (no observed case), body, eyebrow, label, fine-print, mono (uppercase/tabular content has no register to flip).

highlight.$description: Step up exactly one rung within the SAME family (e.g. titleMedium -> titleLarge) to mark the single emphasized instance in an otherwise-repeating list — the next/upcoming item, today's row, the unread one. Creates no new token: it is a usage rule ('render this instance one rung larger'), not a value. Applies to: title (confirmed — DiscussionsTimeline 'next' discussion). Headline is plausible but unconfirmed; body/caption/label/eyebrow/fine-print/mono have no observed case.

display.$description: Hero/editorial scale. Serif, bold, roman only (no feature modifier observed). Reserved for wide-viewport web contexts with room to be editorial (marketing hero, desktop club masthead) — mobile does not use this family; it tops out at Headline. Same three numbers apply everywhere this family is used, on any platform.

medium.$description: Desktop club-detail masthead (kluvs-frontend ClubDetailPage.tsx, desktop split-view).

headline.$description: Page-level identity text — the single biggest 'this page is about X' element. Serif, medium weight, roman by default; feature modifier (italic) confirmed in real use for empty-states and 'the featured thing' framed at headline scale.

medium.$description: e.g. kluvs-frontend BooksPage 'My Shelf' header (responsive 32-38px, this is the normalized rung).

large.$description: Page-hero identity — profile name, mobile club-detail masthead, and the stat-value numbers on Profile (same shape, different content — a number is not a separate tier).

title.$description: Card/row/list-level identity — smaller than Headline, still identity content (a name), not body prose. Serif, medium/regular weight, roman by DEFAULT. feature modifier (italic) is the most heavily-used modifier in the whole system: roman = structural identity (club name in a list), italic = the featured/current thing (book title, session title). highlight modifier (step up one rung) confirmed for the singular emphasized item in a repeating list.

medium.$description: Standard card/list title — club name (roman) or book/session title (+feature, italic). Was 'card-heading' pre-v2, which was already italic-by-default — this generalizes that into title+feature rather than a fixed style.

large.$description: Larger title-scale identity, e.g. a session/discussion title (+feature).

body.$description: Reading content — sans, regular weight. No feature/highlight modifier observed; this is plain prose.

large.$description: Primary reading content — author names, roster/member-name lists. Was 'body-lg' pre-v2.

medium.$description: General supporting sentence-level content. Was 'body' pre-v2.

caption.$description: Sans, regular weight, muted/secondary color baked into the rung (unlike Body, which takes color from context). Metadata: counts, timestamps, membership lines, percentages. feature modifier (italic) confirmed for short asides framed as 'featured' info ('3 books in progress').

eyebrow.$description: Standalone family, not a rung of Label — its defining shape (uppercase + wide tracking) has no equivalent at any other size in the system, so it doesn't belong on a size ladder with non-uppercase siblings. The single most-reused shape found in the whole frontend audit: section headers, modal titles, status/role badges, stat-value labels, interactive pill labels. Color is always supplied externally (secondary/neutral default, copper for active emphasis, role colors for owner/admin) — never baked into the family itself. Historical note: Material 2 had an equivalent dedicated 'overline' style; Material 3 folded it into labelSmall. Kluvs is deliberately following the Material 2 model here because this shape is too distinct from Label to share a ladder with it.

tracking.$description: CSS letter-spacing. Canonical value — most real instances converge here; smaller values found in the wild (0.02-0.12em) are drift toward this same target, not intentional variants.

label.$description: Plain UI chrome text — sentence case, no tracking. Covers nav items and button/CTA text (measured identical in real usage, no separate 'button' style needed). Only one rung confirmed so far; a 'large' rung is a plausible future need (nothing in the audit required it yet) but should not be invented without a real case.

fine-print.$description: Standalone family (not a Caption rung) — smallest, most muted text in the system. Version numbers, disclaimers.

mono.$description: Standalone family for tabular/numeric metadata. See font-family.mono for the current system-stack placeholder.

button.$description: Button system — five variants: Primary (filled), Outlined, Text/Ghost, Text Destructive, and Social (provider-branded OAuth). All M3 variants use colorScheme tokens and adapt to light/dark automatically. Social buttons have fixed provider colors and work on both surfaces.

text.$description: White on copper. 3.53:1 contrast — documented exception. Do not use colorScheme.background as text color.
Destructive action. Always paired with a cancel/dismiss text button.

loading-pattern.$description: Current pattern. Future: animated Kluvs mark SVG rotating.

secondary.$description: Ghost/outlined secondary button — for adjacent secondary actions (e.g. 'Update' beside a progress bar, 'Edit' in a card header). Web class: .kluvs-btn-secondary.

pill.$description: Tiny rounded-full outlined chip for compact inline actions (e.g. 'Copy Club ID'). Distinct from secondary — smaller, fully rounded, supports a transient 'success' state. See docs/buttons.md.

read-ribbon.$description: Diagonal corner-banner marking a book cover as 'read'/finished. Web class: .kluvs-read-ribbon + a size modifier, scaled proportionally to the matching component.book-cover size. See docs/book-cover.md.

shape.$description: Notched banner — wide chevron cut on the inner edge.

read-badge.$description: Circular outline badge marking a book/session as 'read'/finished — used where a corner ribbon doesn't fit (e.g. compact list rows). Web class: .kluvs-read-badge. See docs/book-cover.md.

icon.$description: 16px Kluvs hexagon glyph, matches brand mark.

modal.$description: Three-zone dialog shell — Header / Body / Footer (+ optional DangerZone between Body and Footer). Variants: default (copper eyebrow) and destructive (danger eyebrow). See docs/modal.md for full anatomy spec and platform notes.

label-color-default.$description: color.brand.primary — copper eyebrow for edit/info modals.

cancel-style.$value: ghost text, secondary color, hover → primary

action-style.$value: filled button (bg-primary or bg-danger), rounded-btn, text-white

loading-pattern.$value: KluvsSpinner size=14 color=#ffffff + '…' suffix on label

book-cover.$description: Standardized 2:3 aspect ratio slot for book covers.

ratio.$description: The strict aspect ratio for all book covers.

avatar.$description: Generated member avatar — circular, initials fallback, deterministic hue per user. Role is never encoded on the avatar itself (no ring, no badge) — see component.role-eyebrow. See docs/avatars.md.

initials.$value: 1-2 letters, EB Garamond, cream on dark / dark-chocolate on light
initials.$description: First+last initial if name has 2+ words, else first 2 chars. Text color is foreground-warm.primary (cream) on dark, inverted to color.warm-dark.base (dark chocolate) on light — same swap as the surface backgrounds.

own-color.$description: color.brand.primary — overrides hue palette when avatar represents the current user.

hue-palette.$description: Thematic 12-color palette. Chocolate hues on dark surfaces, Cream hues on light surfaces. Color picked via userId modulo palette length.

avatar-stack.$description: Overlapping row of avatars (e.g. club member preview) with a '+N' overflow chip. See docs/avatars.md.

overlap.$description: Negative margin-left on all but the first avatar.

stack-order.$value: First avatar on top, descending z-index thereafter (z-index 4..1 for up to 3 avatars + overflow chip).

ring.$description: Separates overlapping avatars from their background.

max-shown.$description: Avatars shown before collapsing into the '+N' chip.

overflow-chip.$value: same size as avatar (md), background = track color, text = label color, '+N'

progress-bar.$description: Reading-progress indicator — thin fill bar + label row. Shipped as ProgressRow. NOTE: an in-progress exploration of richer treatments lives in preview/explore-reading-progress.html — this token group reflects the CURRENT shipped version only. See docs/states.md.

label-row.$value: left: optional book title (italic, EB Garamond) or eyebrow label; right: progress text in color.brand.primary, IBM Plex Sans 12px

segmented-control.$description: Pill-shaped multi-option toggle — equal-width segments in a rounded-full bordered container, divided by 1px borders. Two known variants. See docs/buttons.md.

variant-filled.$description: Track-By (Page/Percent) toggle in ReadingProgressModal — active segment fills with brand primary.

variant-status-icon.$description: RSVP attendance control (AttendanceControl) — icon-only segments, active segment tinted by semantic status color (success/neutral/danger).

light-surface.$description: Override via [data-surface="light"] .kluvs-segmented in colors_and_type.css. Fixed-width icon segments size to content (width: auto) on the container regardless of surface.

empty-state.$description: Page-level 'nothing here' state — illustration + message + optional CTA, centered. See docs/states.md.

layout.$value: flex column, centered, gap 24px, py-16 (lg: py-24)

illustration.$value: component.empty-state.stacked-covers (book contexts) — other contexts may omit.

body.$value: 13px, IBM Plex Sans, color.dark-web.content-meta, line-height 1.6, max-width 340px, centered

stacked-covers.$description: Three tilted placeholder covers (book-shaped rects with diagonal-stripe fill) fanned out — used as the illustration for empty book lists/shelves.

book-cover-placeholder.$description: 'No cover available' fallback fill for a single CoverSlot/BookCover — a tessellating hexagon 'hive' grid, optionally with a small mono label (e.g. 'NO COVER').

fill.$description: Inline tessellating-hexagon SVG pattern, stroked with currentColor. See docs/book-cover.md for markup.

role-eyebrow.$description: Shipped role indicator — uppercase label with optional leading dot. SUPERSEDES the avatar-ring + corner-dot pattern in preview/components-member-row.html, which was never implemented. See docs/members.md.

light-surface.$description: Override via [data-surface="light"] .kluvs-role-eyebrow--admin / --member in colors_and_type.css. Owner color is shared across surfaces (validated AA on both).

admin.$description: admin-on-dark fails AA on light; use the base admin teal instead.

member.$description: Inverse of the dark-mode cream — same swap as component.avatar.initials.
